record.paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For completely positive trace-preserving (CPT) maps Φ: M_{d1} → M_{d2}, let E(d1,d2) denote the extreme points of the convex set of such channels, and let the closure of E(d1,d2) consist exactly of the CPT maps whose Choi matrix has rank at most d1. How can one characterize, classify, or parameterize this closure for all input dimensions d1 > 2 and arbitrary output dimensions d2?

evidence.quote: Let E(d1,d2) denote the extreme points of the convex set of CPT maps from Md1 to Md2. Theorem 1. The closure E(d1,d2) of the set of extreme points of CPT maps Φ : Md1 ↦→ Md2 is precisely the set of such maps with Choi rank at most d1.
Problem 1. Characterize, classify and/or parameterize the closure E(d1,d2) of the set of extreme points of CPT maps Φ : Md1 ↦→ Md2 for d1 > 2 and d2 arbitrary.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M_d$ denote the algebra of $d\times d$ complex matrices. A linear map $\Phi: M_{d_1} \to M_{d_2}$ is called completely positive and trace-preserving (CPT) if $\Phi \otimes \mathrm{id}_{M_n}$ maps positive semidefinite matrices to positive semidefinite matrices for every $n \ge 1$, and $\mathrm{tr}(\Phi(X)) = \mathrm{tr}(X)$ for all $X \in M_{d_1}$. The set of CPT maps from $M_{d_1}$ to $M_{d_2}$ is convex; let $\mathcal{E}(d_1,d_2)$ denote its set of extreme points.

The Choi matrix of $\Phi$ is $C(\Phi) = \sum_{i,j=1}^{d_1} E_{ij} \otimes \Phi(E_{ij}) \in M_{d_1} \otimes M_{d_2}$, where $\{E_{ij}\}$ are the standard matrix units. The Choi rank of $\Phi$ is the rank of $C(\Phi)$, equivalently the minimal number of Kraus operators in a representation $\Phi(X) = \sum_k A_k X A_k^*$.

It is known that the closure $\overline{\mathcal{E}(d_1,d_2)}$ in the topology of the convex set of CPT maps coincides exactly with the set of CPT maps $\Phi: M_{d_1} \to M_{d_2}$ whose Choi rank is at most $d_1$.

Problem: For every $d_1 > 2$ and every $d_2 \ge 1$, give an explicit characterization, classification, or parameterization of the closure $\overline{\mathcal{E}(d_1,d_2)}$ — equivalently, of all CPT maps $\Phi: M_{d_1} \to M_{d_2}$ with Choi rank at most $d_1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The case $d_1 = 2$ admits an explicit Kraus parameterization, but for $d_1 > 2$ the problem of characterizing/parameterizing the closure of extreme CPT maps (equivalently, CPT maps with Choi rank at most $d_1$) appears still open. Subsequent work by Ruskai and others (e.g., on extreme points of unital quantum channels) addresses partial cases but not a full parameterization.

status_evidence.snippet: Complete classification of extreme CPT maps for d1=2.
status_evidence.claim: The d1=2 case is fully solved, providing the baseline parameterization.
